readMe.purpose: Index and structural fingerprint of the 62 official NPHIES sample messages.
howToUseThis: byUseCase[useCaseId] -> the paths of every golden sample for that use case.
A sample with superseded:true is a re-dated copy; build against its supersededBy path.
samples[].fingerprint holds what the file ACTUALLY contains. Where it and the Confluence prose disagree, the disagreement is the finding — neither side wins automatically.
violations[] lists every place a golden sample breaks its own format. Several of these are defects in the samples, not NPHIES rules. Do not compile them into validator rules.
headlineFindings: All 5 Raqeeb medication samples are NOT valid JSON: they carry '///' comments, and MedicationRequestBundle_Raqeeb_SplitDosing_19052025.json additionally leaves an object unclosed. No off-the-shelf FHIR parser reads them as shipped.

'occurencePeriod' (one r) outnumbers the correct 'occurrencePeriod' 33 to 5 across the lab/rad attachment bundles. The 27-01-2026 re-issues fix only the first occurrence in each file. Same story for 'effectivedateTime' vs 'effectiveDateTime', 12 to 3.
RadiologyOrderBundle_AuthorPerson_Structured_..._27012026.json — the CANONICAL, newest radiology order — contains the key "occurقencePeriod" with an Arabic QAF (U+0642) wedged into the element name.

ADT_sample03 and ADT_sample04 are escaped-string dumps, not wire format: a literal two-character '\r' ends every segment and MSH.2 reads '^~\\&'. ADT_sample08 is clean. All three declare MSH.12 = '2.5' even though the folder says v2.5.1.

The two-family FHIR rule holds in all 22 bundles with no exception: medication bundles are type 'message' with MessageHeader first, lab/rad attachment bundles are type 'document' with Composition first.
No golden SOAP envelope carries a WS-Security or SAML header, so the golden set gives no evidence whatsoever about the security header — which is also why saml-sso has no sample.

Golden CDA documents reuse ClinicalDocument/id across files (both radiology results share RadioReport123456789; all six on-demand documents share f26a51ee-...), so the XDS DocumentEntry.uniqueId cannot tell them apart.

confidence.high: Everything under samples[].fingerprint — parsed from the bytes on disk.
confidence.adjudicated: elementNameConflicts[].verdict and the FHIR element-shape violations are checked against FHIR R4 base definitions, not against Confluence; each carries a 'basis' field saying so.
confidence.flagged: Anything marked 'needs-review', 'ambiguous' or 'medium' is not settled.
